explanation: Fires on Hispanic, French or Portuguese words and names, and on nationality or place words for those cultures: accented name pieces (Gonz-ález, López, João, Café), Spanish/French place names (Québec, Madrid, Nuevo México), and adjectives like Mexican, French, Colombian, Cuban. Plain English words fire weakly or not at all.

No single theme. The strongest cases are the space before a model or version number in product names (Atari 7800, OnePlus 3, Lupin the 3rd, Galaxy S8), 'and' in 'between X and Y' number ranges, and various prepositions (in/of/for/on) in titles or noun phrases. Activation is broad and hard to predict.

Fires on short function words, mainly 'in' and 'a' (also 'for', 'than', 'such'), that follow a noun phrase and start a prepositional phrase. Typical cases are 'a species of X in the family', 'coffee in the world', 'in a table' and 'In a sense'. Content words do not fire.

A mixture: file and path pieces in code (.min, .component, ./*.), digits inside IDs or timestamps, stock-ticker colons, percent punctuation, and assorted words in prose (air in 'airway', 'suggested', 'where'). There is no clear shared trigger.

Fires on the final token that completes a contrasting or comparison item, e.g. E-select-in, 'atrop-ine' or 'domestically' in 'abroad instead of domestically', 'return' in 'non-matching return value', 'does' in 'X errors but Y does not'. It is very mixed, and the token itself predicts little.

A mixture: infinitive 'to' after nouns or verbs of need or purpose (need to, space to, words to, firm to), the second half of hyphenated compounds (face-to-face, one-on-one, head-on, Non-human), and word-completion subwords in names, URLs and fixed phrases (great time, of all things, PARTICULAR PURPOSE).

A mixture: 'post' in time phrases like '120 h post inoculation', a '?' plus newline that ends a question title, 'in' in 'species of plant in the family', and assorted verbs and objects ('look', 'hold it', 'raise your voice'). There is no consistent trigger.

Fires on tokens just after a structural break or inside numbers and identifiers. Examples are the first token of a new list item or section after newlines, digits inside years, IPs or version numbers (192.[1]68, 1990–[2]009), and subwords inside chemical or technical names. It is diffuse and mostly positional.

Fires strongly on 'year' in 'this year' / 'this year's', and on determiner-modifier words like 'this latter', 'every single', 'several different'. It also fires on tech name pieces (ASP.NET, emberjs, Google+, linux, GDPR). These are two or more unrelated triggers.

Fires in formal technical, patent or scientific prose on its connective words: 'to' in 'relates to' / 'binds to', 'for' in 'accounts for', main verbs such as 'uses' and 'bind', and especially the sentence-final period that closes a background or problem statement ('...clean technologies.', '...IC packages.'). Casual text fires weakly.

Fires at structural boundaries in document headers and boilerplate. Examples are the newline or period after a copyright, license or encoding line, the first 'package'/'namespace'/'class' keyword after a license block, court-case caption lines (Court of Appeal, Circuit newline), and the newline after a math-problem answer. Ordinary body text does not fire.

Fires on verbs of telling, giving, showing or helping that take a person as recipient: 'tell', 'tells', 'give(s)', 'gave', 'show(ed)', 'help', especially in requests like 'Can someone tell me' or 'it gives me'. Weaker on related prepositions ('dawned on me', 'around me').

A mixture of word or phrase completions in technical and boilerplate text: 'version' in '<?xml version', ' *' at the start of license-comment lines, 'notice' in 'copyright notice', COPYING, noqa, and medical subwords (Hyponat-rem-ia, antiarr-hyth-mic). There is no single shared concept.

Two triggers. One is the verb 'come'/'came' in phrasal uses (come across, came up with, came from, come with, came to see). The other is the middle subword of medical compound terms (immun-os-uppressive, lymph-ob-lastic, melan-oc-ortin, immun-om-odulatory).

Fires on the word that completes an idiom or a predictable multiword expression or long word: 'no doubt', 'safe to say', 'everyone knows', 'for once', 'fruitless', 'Morris Maze', 'civil society', 'deacetylase'. The context makes the token highly predictable, but the topics are unrelated.

Fires on tokens inside the names of software tools, frameworks and environments in programming questions and code (XAMPP, Aptana, wamp, JENKINS, TortoiseSVN, Angular, WPF, luaotf, ビルド in 'maven build'). Also fires on indentation and other code tokens. Non-technical text does not fire.

Fires on the second word of a product or tool name or a fixed noun compound: Android Studio, Visual Studio, xcode project, free utility, financial incentive, Node-RED, Higgs. It also fires on other unrelated tokens ('part of', 'Honduras for', 'reached #4 in the'), so it is mixed.

Fires on middle or final subword pieces of medical, anatomical and biological Greek/Latin terms (oes-ophage-al, lary-nge-al, Spl-en-omegaly, acet-ab-ular, cere-bell-ar, rhin-oc-eros, astro-cy-tes) and similar long technical words. Whole common words do not fire.

Fires mainly on 'which' (and 'what') right after a preposition in a relative or indirect clause ('in which', 'under which', 'at which', 'from which method', 'on what type'). There are weaker scattered cases on prepositions or words in restrictive phrases ('until', 'under-21', 'such as').

Fires on existential 'there' / 'There' in 'there is/are/has been/might be', especially after a discourse connective (However, there...; Currently, there...; and there...). It fires moderately on presentational 'here' ('Here is/are') and 'there' in questions, and weakly on sentence-initial 'It'.

Fires most strongly on the space between an abbreviated month or 'Fig' and the following number (Jan 01, Feb 20, Aug 2018, JUL 18, Fig 1). It also fires on continuation subwords inside words or names (blastosp-ores, Col-oured, St-over, inf-ographic) and moderately on sentence-ending periods. It is a mixture.
